source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text: When selecting durian planting material, this source advises growers to prioritize a few practical criteria over fruit-name reputation alone: choose planting stock (grafted seedlings, ideally) from a known, healthy mother tree with a track record of reliable yield and good fruit quality in conditions similar to the grower's own site; avoid seedlings showing any sign of disease, weak growth, or root damage in the nursery bag; and consider the local market's preferred variety and flesh characteristics (sweetness, color, seed size, aroma intensity) since these vary by variety and strongly affect the price the fruit can fetch. Grafted planting material is preferred over seed-grown trees because grafted trees begin bearing fruit substantially sooner and reliably reproduce the fruit quality of the known mother tree, whereas a seed-grown tree can take many more years to bear and its fruit quality is unpredictable since durian does not breed true from seed.
